SUMMARY 
 
• Data Engineer with 8+ years of experience designing, developing, optimizing, and supporting enterprise data engineering and data warehousing 
solutions, with strong hands-on expertise in Snowflake, SQL, Python, ETL/ELT, dbt, and Apache Airflow.

delivering scalable data solutions for financial, risk, regulatory, and analytics reporting.

and cloud-native orchestration services. 
• Proficient in building distributed data processing frameworks using PySpark, SQL, and Python, enabling scalable ingestion, 
transformation, and analytics across enterprise datasets. 
• Experienced in building distributed Spark pipelines using both PySpark and Scala 2.x, applying functional transformation patterns across 
Spark Dataset and DataFrame APIs to support scalable batch and streaming analytics workloads across Dataproc and EMR 
environments.

formats, and governance controls. 
• Hands-on experience developing RESTful APIs using FastAPI and integrating data services with microservice architectures using Docker 
and Kubernetes. 
• Strong understanding of dimensional modeling (Kimball methodology), data warehousing, and data governance frameworks 
supporting enterprise analytics and reporting. 
• Experienced in implementing secure data access controls, IAM policies, RBAC governance, and encryption mechanisms for regulated 
healthcare and financial datasets. 
• Skilled in CI/CD automation and production observability for cloud-native data platforms using GitHub Actions, Cloud Composer, 
Terraform (IaC), Prometheus, and Grafana. 
• Collaborative engineer experienced in working with cross-functional teams including analytics, platform engineering, and data science teams 
to deliver reliable and scalable data solutions. 
 
SKILLS 
  
 Languages & Frameworks: Python, SQL, PySpark, Scala (2.x), Shell Scripting, FastAPI, Pydantic, DBT 
Cloud Platforms: Google Cloud Platform (BigQuery, Dataflow, Cloud Composer, Dataproc, GKE, Vertex AI, Cloud Logging, Cloud Monitoring), AWS 
Data Engineering: Apache Spark, PySpark, Kafka, Flink, BigQuery, Dataproc, Dataflow, Snowflake, AWS Glue 
Data Platforms & Storage: BigQuery, Delta Lake, Amazon S3, Snowflake, Redshift, DynamoDB, Azure Blob Storage  
AI / ML Platforms: Vertex AI, MLflow, DataRobot (model scoring pipeline integration), RAG pipelines, TensorFlow  
Analytics & Visualization: Looker, Looker Studio, Tableau, Power BI 
Search & Observability: OpenSearch (Elasticsearch), Kibana, Prometheus, Grafana, Cloud Monitoring

Data Security & Governance: IAM, RBAC, KMS Encryption, Token Masking, Lake Formation, Unity Catalog, HIPAA, GDPR 
Tools: Jira, Postman, Swagger/OpenAPI, Visual Studio Code, SQL Workbench 
 
WORK EXPERIENCE 
 
Intuit, Credit Karma – Charlotte, NC / May 2026 - present 
GCP Data Engineer 
Project: On Intuit's Credit Karma Partner Enrollment platform, I build and maintain event-driven ETL/ELT pipelines that enroll users in near real-
time across major credit bureaus (TransUnion, Experian, Equifax), alongside error-classification and observability tooling that gives analytics 
teams and downstream clients clear visibility into enrollment outcomes. 
• Build and maintain Python-based ETL/ELT pipelines integrated with GCP Pub/Sub event streams, powering near real-time enrollment 
data ingestion across bureau services (TransUnion, Experian, Equifax) through the Partner Enrollment Service and Partner Data Service. 
• Re-architect core ingestion components to improve pipeline reliability, scalability, and observability, reducing failure points across high-
throughput bureau enrollment workflows. 
• Own the Error Standardization initiative end-to-end: design and implement classification logic for non-retryable bureau enrollment errors 
and publish results to curated BigQuery tables. 
• Partner with offline analytics teams and downstream clients to translate error-classification output into clear visibility into why specific 
users cannot be enrolled, reducing support escalations. 
• Write and optimize complex SQL for data ingestion, transformation, validation, and troubleshooting across high-volume bureau datasets 
operating in a PII-heavy, compliance-sensitive environment. 

• Ensure accuracy and consistency of enrollment and error-classification logic through rigorous SQL-based validation and reconciliation 
checks against bureau source data. 
• Develop and integrate custom AI-assisted development workflows using Claude Code directly into bureau service codebases to accelerate 
feature implementation and reduce delivery time. 
• Strengthen unit and integration test coverage and code quality using AI-assisted tooling, and actively participate in code reviews and Git-
based PR workflows to uphold engineering standards. 
• Ship changes through GitHub Actions CI/CD pipelines and validate pipeline correctness post-deployment to ensure safe, reliable releases 
into production. 
• Leverage Falcon-based service instrumentation and New Relic monitoring/alerting to support production on-call response, proactively 
identifying and escalating blockers. 
• Design and maintain BigQuery table schemas and event contracts for the Partner Enrollment and Partner Data Services, ensuring consistent, 
well-documented data structures for downstream analytics and client consumption. 
• Build dashboards and alerting thresholds on top of Falcon and New Relic metrics to track enrollment success/failure rates and error-
classification trends in real time, giving engineering and analytics teams early visibility into platform health. 
• Partner with backend and platform engineering teams on service architecture decisions for the bureau enrollment pipeline and contribute to 
technical documentation and onboarding materials to support team scalability. 
• Developed and optimized Python/SQL-based data pipelines in BigQuery and cloud data platforms, implementing data validation, 
reconciliation, and transformation logic for large-scale financial and credit datasets. 
• Supported production data pipelines through GitHub Actions CI/CD, monitoring, troubleshooting, and root-cause analysis, partnering with 
analytics and business teams to deliver reliable data for credit and risk reporting. 
 
CVS Health, Aetna -  Dallas, Texas / September 2025 – April 2026 
GCP Data Engineer

by consolidating healthcare datasets including claims, transcripts, and survey data into a unified real-time data platform supporting personalized 
member interactions and operational insights. 
• Architected and implemented scalable ETL pipelines within the SAGA AI platform, onboarding 20+ batch and near-real-time pipelines

Name: Nitish Rao B

Linkedin: : https://www.linkedin.com/in/nitishraobo/|| Phone: 4692696680| mailto:nitishb2317@gmail.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY:

Over 10+ years of professional IT experience as a Big Data Engineer, consistently building and improving scalable data solutions across healthcare, financial services, manufacturing, and consumer credit sectors, delivering measurable and lasting business impact at enterprise scale.

Designed and maintained enterprise-scale Scala and Apache Spark 2.x/3.x applications supporting Medicaid Encounter Processing pipelines, covering Provider Data, Member Data, Encounter Data, and Reference Data with full end-to-end reliability across mission-critical downstream systems.

Took full technical ownership of the Drools business rules engine, handling rule authoring, versioning, testing, and ongoing maintenance to enforce Medicaid Claims adjudication logic within the Scala/Spark application framework throughout the complete rule lifecycle.

Built and fine-tuned Apache Spark batch workflows using Spark Core, Spark SQL, Spark DataFrame, Spark Dataset, and Spark RDD, diagnosing performance bottlenecks through Spark UI and Spark History Server to consistently meet enterprise SLA requirements for high-volume Encounter Data.

Administered the full Cloudera Data Platform environment spanning Cloudera Data Engineering, Cloudera Data Warehouse, Cloudera DataFlow, Cloudera Manager, HDFS, YARN, Hue, Ranger, and Atlas to maintain platform availability, security, and continuity of production Medicaid workloads.

Handled enterprise data ingestion for master data and source system files using Apache Hive 3.x, Apache Sqoop, Apache Flume, and Apache NiFi, ensuring accurate and timely loading of Medicaid Eligibility, Member Data, and Reference Data into the distributed data environment.

Investigated and resolved production incidents for Spark on YARN distributed workloads using Spark History Server, Spark UI, DataDog, Grafana, Prometheus, and ELK Stack, conducting root cause analysis to restore system stability with minimal downtime impact.

Coordinated production releases and deployment pipelines through Git, Bitbucket, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and Maven, maintaining structured SBT build workflows and Scala packaging processes for controlled deployments into Linux-based production environments.

Refined SQL processing logic across Apache Hive, Apache Impala, and Spark SQL by applying advanced query tuning techniques that improved batch throughput and reduced processing time for large-scale Medicaid Claims, Encounter Data, and Provider Data datasets.

Connected the Scala/Spark application framework with IBM DataStage and Apache Kafka to support enterprise data exchange and streaming ingestion, maintaining reliable data flow between source systems, HDFS, and downstream Medicaid reporting and claims processing systems.

Validated pipeline accuracy and data quality across Medicaid Encounter Processing stages using ScalaTest, Pytest, Unittest, and Great Expectations, covering Drools business rule outputs and Spark DataFrame transformations through comprehensive unit and integration test coverage.

Supported AWS infrastructure components including Amazon S3, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, and Amazon Kinesis, coordinating with cloud operations teams to maintain secure integration between on-premise CDP workloads and AWS-hosted services.

Built and maintained ETL orchestration pipelines using Apache Airflow and Apache Oozie to manage scheduling, dependency resolution, and failure recovery for Spark, Hive, and HBase workflows running across enterprise Medicaid data processing operations on YARN.

Developed supporting data engineering utilities, automation scripts, and validation tools using Python, PySpark, Pandas, NumPy, SQLAlchemy, Boto3, and Requests to complement the core Scala/Spark framework and improve operational efficiency across Medicaid Claims workflows.

Maintained data governance and metadata management activities using Apache Atlas, Collibra, Alation, and Erwin, documenting data lineage and enforcing data stewardship policies for Medicaid Eligibility, Provider Data, Member Data, and Reference Data assets across the enterprise platform.

Defined and maintained data models and schema structures using ER/Studio, Power Designer, and Erwin for Apache Hive, HBase, and Snowflake, ensuring Medicaid Encounter Processing data aligned with enterprise standards and downstream reporting requirements across all tiers.

Provisioned and managed Linux-based server environments through Terraform, Ansible, and Jenkins pipelines, supporting consistent and repeatable deployment of Cloudera Data Platform components and the Scala/Spark application framework across development, staging, and production environments.

Maintained working knowledge of Apache Beam, Amazon DynamoDB, Amazon RDS, AWS Lambda, Informatica PowerCenter, Talend, SSIS, Pentaho, and Apache Storm to evaluate integration options and provide informed technical guidance during architecture discussions for Medicaid data processing initiatives.

Cloud Environment: GCP (Cloud storage, Bigquery, DataProc, Functions, GKE, Spanner), AWS (Redshift, EMR, Glue, S3, Lambda, Athena, Snowflake, EC2, RDS, Cloud Watch, VPC, SQS, Jenkins), Azure (Databricks, Data lake, Data factory, Blob storage, SQL, HDInsight, Fabric, CosmosDB)

Big Data Ecosystem: Spark, Hive, Kafka, HDFS, Airflow, NiFi, Spark Streaming, Sqoop, Flume, MapReduce, Yarn, Zookeeper

Programming languages: Python, Java, Scala, Pyspark, Spring boot, SQL, T-SQL, Unix

resume.resumeText:
>     	                 q           s               p                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        	                     wX    bjbjf f                   	   .     {k  {kwP                                                                                                                                                                                4                    #  t   f       |       |       |       |       k       k       k        "       "       "       "       "       "       "      v$      ,'  \    "                              k                       k       k       k       k        "                              |               |        "      3       3       3       k               |               |        "              3                                                       k        "              3       3   :   =!  <                                                                            !      |               0   A                  )       y!  
            "       "  0    #       !  R    '      #        '       !                                                                               '                       !      k       k       3       k       k                                       k       k       k        "       "                                                                              k       k       k        #      k       k       k       k                                                                                                                                                                '      k       k       k       k       k       k                                                               k       k       k           X   X   :         	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       POOJA YADAVSenior Data EngineerPhone: 716-775-7940Email:  HYPERLINK "mailto:rk@cleoconsult.com" rk@cleoconsult.com  (K. Ramesh) PROFESSIONAL SUMMARYSr. Data engineer with 10+ years building and running data pipelines and warehouses, mostly on AWS and Azure, across healthcare, banking, retail, telecom, and insurance. Spend most of my time in Python, SQL, and PySpark   building batch and streaming pipelines with Kafka, Airflow, and Spark, and warehousing on Snowflake, Redshift, and Synapse. Comfortable owning something end-to-end: ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and the data quality/governance work that keeps it trustworthy once it's in production. Have led a small team and mentored a couple of junior engineers, but still prefer being hands-on with the code most days. Worked mainly in Agile teams, usually as the person other engineers come to when a pipeline breaks at 2am.TECHNICAL SKILLSProgramming Languages Python, SQL, Scala, Java  Big Data Technologies Apache Spark, PySpark, Hadoop, Hive, Kafka, HBase, Apache Phoenix, Pig, Delta Lake  Cloud Platforms AWS, Microsoft Azure, Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, ADLS Gen2, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure SQL Database, S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, Redshift, Athena, IAM, CloudWatch, Step Functions, Azure Data Factory (ADF), Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2), Synapse Analytics, Azure SQL Database,Azure Event Hubs,Analytics, Azure Key Vault.  Data Warehousing Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Azure Synapse Analytics, SQL Server, Oracle  ETL & Data Integration Apache Airflow, Azure Data Factory, SSIS, DBT, Sqoop, Oozie, Informatica (legacy)  Streaming Technologies Apache Kafka, Spark Streaming  Databases SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB  DevOps & Version Control Git, GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, TFS  Visualization & Reporting Power BI, SSRS, SSAS, Microsoft Excel  Methodologies & Tools Agile (Scrum), Jira, Azure DevOps, Linux/Unix  WORK EXPERIENCESenior Data EngineerUnitedHealth Group | Minnetonka, MN	                                                 Jan 2024   PresentOwn the ingestion and transformation layer for a claims/pharmacy/provider/member data platform that processes north of 12TB a day across three business units.Rebuilt the EHR-to-analytics ingestion path that used to run as a set of one-off scripts into a metadata-driven Glue/EMR framework   cut onboarding time for a new source system from about two weeks to 2-3 days.Sit with healthcare architects roughly biweekly to design shared data products for quality measures and member risk scoring so downstream teams stop rebuilding the same tables.Applied Unity Catalog-based governance patterns for controlled access to analytical datasets, supporting centralized permissions, data discovery and audit requirements.Built a reconciliation job that compares row/hash counts between source claims systems and the Snowflake warehouse nightly   caught several silent data-loss issues that used to surface as bad reports weeks later.Migrated four legacy regulatory reporting extracts into Snowflake, including clustering key redesign that dropped average query time from ~40s to under 10s on the largest fact table.Worked with MongoDB as a source for semi-structured healthcare data and integrated document-based datasets into downstream data pipelines.Designed and maintained Snowflake dimensional data models for claims, member, provider and pharmacy datasets, supporting analytical reporting and downstream healthcare data products.Designed a config-driven ingestion framework (JSON-defined source mappings) so new healthcare feeds can be onboarded without a code deploy   currently running 40+ sources through it.Developed fact and dimension tables using star-schema principles and optimized Snowflake clustering, pruning and warehouse sizing for high-volume healthcare workloads.Used Databricks Workflows to orchestrate notebook-based transformation jobs and dependent data-processing tasks across development and production environments.Developed reusable ETL frameworks for structured and semi-structured data, including source-to-target mappings, incremental processing, data validation, error handling, and reconciliation.Established baseline runtime and throughput benchmarks for high-volume Spark and Airflow pipelines, tracking processing latency, failure rates, and SLA adherence to identify capacity and performance issues before production impact.Developed Spark jobs in Java to perform ETL from SQL Server to Hadoop.Wrote the first set of DBT models for the quality-reporting team, including tests for null checks and referential integrity that previously didn't exist.Tuned Spark and Databricks workloads by addressing partitioning, join skew, and resource configuration issues, improving processing time for high-volume production pipelines.Profiled and re-partitioned several of the heaviest Spark jobs (skewed joins on member ID)   got end-to-end runtime down about 45% on the biggest one.Worked with the cloud cost team on Snowflake warehouse sizing and auto-suspend settings; helped bring monthly compute spend down without hurting SLAs.Handle HIPAA-related data controls for the pipelines I own   row-level masking for PHI fields, access logging, and lineage documentation for audit requests.Designed HBase schema based on data access patterns. Used Phoenix to add SQL layer on HBase table. Created indexes on Phoenix tables for optimization.Wrote Terraform modules for the team's EMR cluster provisioning and S3 bucket policies; these now get reused by two other pods.Implemented automated data-quality checks across source-to-target healthcare pipelines to identify missing records, duplicate claims, schema inconsistencies and reconciliation failures.Established metadata and lineage documentation for critical healthcare datasets used in regulatory and quality-reporting workflows.Put together feature tables for the data science team's member-engagement model   mostly aggregation and windowing logic on top of the claims data I already own.Environment: AWS Glue, AWS EMR, S3, Snowflake, PySpark, Spark, Python, Apache Airflow, Kafka, DBT, Terraform, Redshift, Lambda, Athena, Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Jira, AgileLead Data EngineerJPMorgan Chase | Plano, TX	Apr 2021   Dec 2023Led a 5-person data engineering pod responsible for the fraud-analytics and risk-reporting data lake; split time roughly 60/40 between hands-on development and reviewing the team's PRs/design docs.Rewrote the core transaction-processing pipeline in PySpark   was handling a few hundred million records a day, now comfortably clears a billion+ on peak days without falling behind schedule.Designed the ingestion framework banking app teams use to onboard new transactional and reference data feeds; before this, each new feed was a custom one-off build taking a sprint or more.Performed data validation and source-to-target reconciliation across MongoDB and analytical data stores.Built the Kafka-based streaming layer that feeds the near-real-time fraud scoring service   worked closely with the fraud team's ML engineers on schema and latency requirements.Regular point of contact for the risk management group on stress-testing and capital-planning data   sat in on their planning meetings so I understood requirements before they hit my backlog.Integrated MongoDB document data with relational and Kafka-based transaction sources, using PySpark and Spark SQL for transformation, validation, and downstream fraud analytics.Worked with application and risk teams to define pipeline SLAs and operational thresholds for transaction-processing workloads, using runtime and throughput metrics to guide Spark tuning and capacity planning.Developed optimized star-schema data marts supporting fraud analytics, AML monitoring and regulatory reporting requirements.Used Spark SQL along with PySpark and Scala to transform high-volume transaction data used by fraud analytics and risk-reporting applications.Applied AWS IAM controls to data lake resources containing transaction and customer information, working within the bank's security and access-control standards.Used CloudWatch monitoring and application logs to troubleshoot failed data-processing jobs and investigate pipeline issues affecting reporting SLAs.Supported Redshift data models and reporting datasets used for fraud analytics, risk reporting, and regulatory data certification.Used Jenkins-based CI/CD processes to package and promote data-processing changes across development and production environments.Ran the multi-quarter migration off legacy Informatica ETL onto Spark on EMR; wrote most of the migration runbooks and did side-by-side validation on the higher-risk workloads myself.Owned Airflow scheduling and dependency management for the team's DAGs, including on-call for SLA breaches.Built the reconciliation and data-quality checks that feed into the bank's data certification sign-off process; presented results to compliance stakeholders quarterly.Participated in DR planning and production readiness reviews for the fraud platform, including a failover test that surfaced a gap in our S3 replication config.Mentored two junior engineers on the team   code reviews, pairing on their first ingestion pipelines, that kind of thing.Environment: AWS EMR, S3, Spark, Scala, PySpark, Kafka, Hive, HDFS, Airflow, Redshift, Python, Jenkins, Git, Docker, SQL, Oracle, Unix, AgileData EngineerWalmart Inc. | Bentonville, AR	Jan 2018   Mar 2021Built and maintained pipelines feeding inventory, sales, customer, and supply-chain analytics for the merchandising org   my first real production ownership after the Verizon contract.Moved a good chunk of our ETL from on-prem SSIS-style jobs to Azure Data Factory + Databricks over about a year; picked up Delta Lake along the way once it became the team standard for the lake layer.Designed star-schema and dimensional data models supporting Power BI reporting for merchandising and executive-level business reviews.Used Azure DevOps for source control, CI/CD coordination, deployment tracking, and release management across ADF and Databricks workloads.Designed Azure Synapse dimensional models for sales, inventory, product, supplier and customer analytics using fact and dimension tables.Optimized SQL and Spark workloads by tuning joins, partitioning, data skew, and query logic, reducing a high-volume retail transformation from approximately 50 minutes to under 15 minutes.Built the transformation framework that pulls together supplier, product catalog, and inventory data from a handful of source systems that didn't always agree with each other on product IDs   spent a lot of time on entity resolution logic here.Worked with MongoDB for semi-structured product, supplier, and inventory data, supporting ingestion and downstream analytics workflows.Wrote PySpark jobs against multi-terabyte sales/inventory tables; built out star-schema models that the BI team's Power BI reports still run on.Developed reusable enterprise data warehouse structures integrating retail transaction, inventory and product master data for Power BI reporting.Worked with Delta Lake tables in Azure Databricks to manage sales, inventory, supplier, and product datasets used by downstream analytics teams.Used Spark SQL and PySpark to transform multi-terabyte retail datasets and prepare curated data for merchandising and supply-chain reporting.Applied medallion-style data architecture using Delta Lake across raw, transformed, and curated layers, improving data quality and reuse for downstream analytics.Used Azure Stream Analytics to process near-real-time retail event data and support timely availability of operational datasets for downstream reporting.Built reusable PySpark and Spark SQL ETL transformations in Databricks for multi-terabyte datasets, including joins, aggregations, cleansing, validation, and incremental processing.Developed Python-based data processing routines to extract and transform MongoDB documents before loading curated datasets into Azure data platforms.Integrated MongoDB product, supplier, and inventory collections with Azure data pipelines, performing source-to-target validation before loading curated datasets into Databricks and Synapse.Optimized Synapse SQL queries and large analytical tables through partitioning, distribution strategy and query tuning.Fixed a recurring data-skew problem on one of our biggest join jobs (a few SKUs had wildly disproportionate transaction volume) by salting the join key   took the job from ~50 min to under 15.Built automated validation checks comparing row counts and key aggregates between source and target after each load; alerted the team via email/Teams when something looked off instead of waiting for someone downstream to notice.Partnered with merchandising and business teams to understand reporting requirements, investigate data discrepancies, and ensure datasets were available for seasonal planning and operational decisions.Helped validate data during a legacy warehouse-to-cloud migration   mostly writing comparison queries and chasing down discrepancies with the DBA team.Performed data validation and reconciliation between MongoDB source collections and downstream Databricks datasets to identify missing or inconsistent records.Built the datasets behind several exec-level Power BI dashboards used in weekly merchandising reviews; iterated on these a lot based on feedback from stakeholders who weren't shy about pointing out what was missing.Used Azure Key Vault to securely manage credentials and connection information for Azure data integration workflows.Developed dimensional and semantic datasets supporting Power BI reporting, aligning business definitions, reusable measures, and analytical models with merchandising requirements.Implemented Azure Key Vault for secure management of credentials and connection information used by data integration workflows.Performed source-to-target validation, reconciliation, and root-cause analysis for pipeline and data-quality issues, resolving discrepancies with source-system and DBA teams.Set up basic pipeline monitoring/alerting so failed ADF jobs got flagged before someone opened a support ticket asking where their report was.Environment: Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS Gen2), PySpark, Spark SQL, Azure SQL Database, Synapse Analytics, Python, Power BI, Git, Azure DevOps, SQL ServerHadoop / Big Data EngineerVerizon | Irving, TX	Jun 2016   Dec 2017Joined the network analytics team as they were moving reporting off Oracle onto Hadoop   mostly wrote ingestion and transformation jobs for customer usage, billing, and network performance data.Redesigned a handful of the largest Hive tables with proper partitioning (by date) and bucketing (by subscriber ID) after query times on the old flat tables were getting complaints from the analytics team.Wrote Hive and Spark jobs against usage/billing/network datasets that ran into the multi-terabyte range; helped plan out the HDFS directory structure and retention policy for the growing data lake.Implemented Kafka ingestion patterns for network-event streams and validated incoming event data before downstream processing.Used Sqoop to pull data out of Oracle into Hadoop on a recurring schedule; tuned split-by columns and parallelism so imports didn't hammer the source database during business hours.Developed Hive-based dimensional data marts for customer usage, network performance and revenue analytics using partitioned and bucketed tables.Used Spark SQL and Hive queries to transform large customer usage, billing, and network-performance datasets stored across HDFS.Worked with HBase for selected high-volume datasets where access patterns required faster lookups than traditional Hive tables.Tuned Kafka ingestion settings for network-event feeds to handle increasing event volumes without affecting the existing batch workloads.Worked with Oracle-to-Hadoop ingestion through Sqoop, validating source-to-target counts and resolving discrepancies during scheduled loads.Built Oozie workflows to chain together the Sqoop imports, Hive transforms, and downstream jobs   this was before Airflow was really an option on our stack.Optimized large-scale Hive queries through partition pruning, bucketing and query-plan tuning across multi-terabyte telecom datasets.Set up a basic Kafka ingestion pipeline for a subset of near-real-time network events, which was fairly new territory for the team at the time.Built out several Hive data marts for churn analysis and revenue reporting that the ops reporting team used directly.Worked with network engineering on service-quality datasets   mostly translating what they wanted to see operationally into something that could actually be queried at scale.Built batch ingestion workflows using Sqoop and Oozie, coordinating Oracle-to-HDFS ingestion, Hive transformations and downstream reporting jobs.FHelped the QA team validate a few large migrations from the old reporting system, mostly spot-checking row counts and aggregates against known-good numbers.Environment: Hadoop, HDFS, Hive, Pig, Sqoop, Oozie, Spark, Kafka, HBase, Python, Shell Scripting, Oracle, Unix/Linux, GitETL Developer / Junior Data EngineerState Farm Insurance | Bloomington, IL	May 2015   May 2016First job out of the gate on the policy/claims reporting team   started out mostly maintaining existing SSIS packages before getting to build new ones.Built parameterized SSIS packages to load policy administration, claims, and customer data from several source systems into SQL Server staging and reporting databases.Put together reusable ETL templates so the underwriting and claims reporting teams didn't need a new package built from scratch every time they onboarded a new report.Used T-SQL to develop stored procedures, views, and transformation logic for policy, claims, and customer reporting datasets.Worked with SQL Server Agent to schedule recurring ETL jobs and configured failure notifications for overnight claims and policy data loads.Used SSIS package variables, parameters, and error-handling components to make recurring insurance data loads easier to maintain.Developed SQL Server data warehouse staging, fact and dimension structures for policy, claims and customer reporting.Supported SSRS reporting for claims operations by validating source data, report queries, and calculated measures before deployment.Worked with Oracle source data during insurance reporting feeds and validated extracts before loading them into SQL Server staging tables.Wrote stored procedures, views, and a fair amount of T-SQL for reporting   learned a lot about query tuning from a senior DBA who reviewed most of my early work.Implemented CDC-based incremental loads on a couple of the larger claims tables after the nightly full-refresh jobs started running past their maintenance window.Built SSRS reports for the claims operations team and helped out on a few SSAS cubes, though that was more the senior developer's area   I mostly supported.Spent a good amount of time on data profiling and cleansing   finding duplicate policy records, inconsistent date formats, that sort of thing   before it became a bigger production issue.Added logging and error handling to the older SSIS packages that didn't have any, which made troubleshooting failed loads much less of a guessing game.Built incremental warehouse loads using CDC-based processing for high-volume claims and policy tables to reduce nightly full-refresh processing.Wrote PowerShell scripts to automate a few recurring manual processes (file archiving, log cleanup) and set up SQL Agent jobs with failure email alerts.Sat in on Agile ceremonies (standups, sprint planning, retros) and got comfortable estimating and scoping my own ETL tasks by the second half of the year.Implemented source-to-target reconciliation and data-quality checks across Oracle source systems and SQL Server warehouse tables.Helped document a few of the ETL workflows and wrote basic runbooks   useful since I was often the one who got asked how something worked six months later.Environment: SQL Server, SSIS, SSRS, SSAS, T-SQL, PowerShell, Excel, Windows Server, Oracle, SQL Developer, Team Foundation Server Ramesh) PROFESSIONAL SUMMARYSr. Data engineer with 10+ years building and running data pipelines and warehouses, mostly on AWS and Azure, across healthcare, banking, retail, telecom, and insurance. Spend most of my time in Python, SQL, and PySpark   building batch and streaming pipelines with Kafka, Airflow, and Spark, and warehousing on Snowflake, Redshift, and Synapse. Comfortable owning something end-to-end: ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and the data quality/governance work that keeps it trustworthy once it's in production. Have led a small team and mentored a couple of junior engineers, but still prefer being hands-on with the code most days. Worked mainly in Agile teams, usually as the person other engineers come to when a pipeline breaks at 2am.TECHNICAL SKILLSProgramming Languages Python, SQL, Scala, Java  Big Data Technologies Apache Spark, PySpark, Hadoop, Hive, Kafka, HBase, Apache Phoenix, Pig, Delta Lake  Cloud Platforms AWS, Microsoft Azure, Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, ADLS Gen2, Azure Synapse Analytics, Azure SQL Database, S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, Redshift, Athena, IAM, CloudWatch, Step Functions, Azure Data Factory (ADF), Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2), Synapse Analytics, Azure SQL Database,Azure Event Hubs,Analytics, Azure Key Vault.  Data Warehousing Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Azure Synapse Analytics, SQL Server, Oracle  ETL & Data Integration Apache Airflow, Azure Data Factory, SSIS, DBT, Sqoop, Oozie, Informatica (legacy)  Streaming Technologies Apache Kafka, Spark Streaming  Databases SQL Server, Oracle, MongoDB  DevOps & Version Control Git, GitHub, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, TFS  Visualization & Reporting Power BI, SSRS, SSAS, Microsoft Excel  Methodologies & Tools Agile (Scrum), Jira, Azure DevOps, Linux/Unix  WORK EXPERIENCESenior Data EngineerUnitedHealth Group | Minnetonka, MN	                                                 Jan 2024   PresentOwn the ingestion and transformation layer for a claims/pharmacy/provider/member data platform that processes north of 12TB a day across three business units.Rebuilt the EHR-to-analytics ingestion path that used to run as a set of one-off scripts into a metadata-driven Glue/EMR framework   cut onboarding time for a new source system from about two weeks to 2-3 days.Sit with healthcare architects roughly biweekly to design shared data products for quality measures and member risk scoring so downstream teams stop rebuilding the same tables.Applied Unity Catalog-based governance patterns for controlled access to analytical datasets, supporting centralized permissions, data discovery and audit requirements.Built a reconciliation job that compares row/hash counts between source claims systems and the Snowflake warehouse nightly   caught several silent data-loss issues that used to surface as bad reports weeks later.Migrated four legacy regulatory reporting extracts into Snowflake, including clustering key redesign that dropped average query time from ~40s to under 10s on the largest fact table.Worked with MongoDB as a source for semi-structured healthcare data and integrated document-based datasets into downstream data pipelines.Designed and maintained Snowflake dimensional data models for claims, member, provider and pharmacy datasets, supporting analytical reporting and downstream healthcare data products.Designed a config-driven ingestion framework (JSON-defined source mappings) so new healthcare feeds can be onboarded without a code deploy   currently running 40+ sources through it.Developed fact and dimension tables using star-schema principles and optimized Snowflake clustering, pruning and warehouse sizing for high-volume healthcare workloads.Used Databricks Workflows to orchestrate notebook-based transformation jobs and dependent data-processing tasks across development and production environments.Developed reusable ETL frameworks for structured and semi-structured data, including source-to-target mappings, incremental processing, data validation, error handling, and reconciliation.Established baseline runtime and throughput benchmarks for high-volume Spark and Airflow pipelines, tracking processing latency, failure rates, and SLA adherence to identify capacity and performance issues before production impact.Developed Spark jobs in Java to perform ETL from SQL Server to Hadoop.Wrote the first set of DBT models for the quality-reporting team, including tests for null checks and referential integrity that previously didn't exist.Tuned Spark and Databricks workloads by addressing partitioning, join skew, and resource configuration issues, improving processing time for high-volume production pipelines.Profiled and re-partitioned several of the heaviest Spark jobs (skewed joins on member ID)   got end-to-end runtime down about 45% on the biggest one.Worked with the cloud cost team on Snowflake warehouse sizing and auto-suspend settings; helped bring monthly compute spend down without hurting SLAs.Handle HIPAA-related data controls for the pipelines I own   row-level masking for PHI fields, access logging, and lineage documentation for audit requests.Designed HBase schema based on data access patterns. Used Phoenix to add SQL layer on HBase table. Created indexes on Phoenix tables for optimization.Wrote Terraform modules for the team's EMR cluster provisioning and S3 bucket policies; these now get reused by two other pods.Implemented automated data-quality checks across source-to-target healthcare pipelines to identify missing records, duplicate claims, schema inconsistencies and reconciliation failures.Established metadata and lineage documentation for critical healthcare datasets used in regulatory and quality-reporting workflows.Put together feature tables for the data science team's member-engagement model   mostly aggregation and windowing logic on top of the claims data I already own.Environment: AWS Glue, AWS EMR, S3, Snowflake, PySpark, Spark, Python, Apache Airflow, Kafka, DBT, Terraform, Redshift, Lambda, Athena, Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Jira, AgileLead Data EngineerJPMorgan Chase | Plano, TX	Apr 2021   Dec 2023Led a 5-person data engineering pod responsible for the fraud-analytics and risk-reporting data lake; split time roughly 60/40 between hands-on development and reviewing the team's PRs/design docs.Rewrote the core transaction-processing pipeline in PySpark   was handling a few hundred million records a day, now comfortably clears a billion+ on peak days without falling behind schedule.Designed the ingestion framework banking app teams use to onboard new transactional and reference data feeds; before this, each new feed was a custom one-off build taking a sprint or more.Performed data validation and source-to-target reconciliation across MongoDB and analytical data stores.Built the Kafka-based streaming layer that feeds the near-real-time fraud scoring service   worked closely with the fraud team's ML engineers on schema and latency requirements.Regular point of contact for the risk management group on stress-testing and capital-planning data   sat in on their planning meetings so I understood requirements before they hit my backlog.Integrated MongoDB document data with relational and Kafka-based transaction sources, using PySpark and Spark SQL for transformation, validation, and downstream fraud analytics.Worked with application and risk teams to define pipeline SLAs and operational thresholds for transaction-processing workloads, using runtime and throughput metrics to guide Spark tuning and capacity planning.Developed optimized star-schema data marts supporting fraud analytics, AML monitoring and regulatory reporting requirements.Used Spark SQL along with PySpark and Scala to transform high-volume transaction data used by fraud analytics and risk-reporting applications.Applied AWS IAM controls to data lake resources containing transaction and customer information, working within the bank's security and access-control standards.Used CloudWatch monitoring and application logs to troubleshoot failed data-processing jobs and investigate pipeline issues affecting reporting SLAs.Supported Redshift data models and reporting datasets used for fraud analytics, risk reporting, and regulatory data certification.Used Jenkins-based CI/CD processes to package and promote data-processing changes across development and production environments.Ran the multi-quarter migration off legacy Informatica ETL onto Spark on EMR; wrote most of the migration runbooks and did side-by-side validation on the higher-risk workloads myself.Owned Airflow scheduling and dependency management for the team's DAGs, including on-call for SLA breaches.Built the reconciliation and data-quality checks that feed into the bank's data certification sign-off process; presented results to compliance stakeholders quarterly.Participated in DR planning and production readiness reviews for the fraud platform, including a failover test that surfaced a gap in our S3 replication config.Mentored two junior engineers on the team   code reviews, pairing on their first ingestion pipelines, that kind of thing.Environment: AWS EMR, S3, Spark, Scala, PySpark, Kafka, Hive, HDFS, Airflow, Redshift, Python, Jenkins, Git, Docker, SQL, Oracle, Unix, AgileData EngineerWalmart Inc. | Bentonville, AR	Jan 2018   Mar 2021Built and maintained pipelines feeding inventory, sales, customer, and supply-chain analytics for the merchandising org   my first real production ownership after the Verizon contract.Moved a good chunk of our ETL from on-prem SSIS-style jobs to Azure Data Factory + Databricks over about a year; picked up Delta Lake along the way once it became the team standard for the lake layer.Designed star-schema and dimensional data models supporting Power BI reporting for merchandising and executive-level business reviews.Used Azure DevOps for source control, CI/CD coordination, deployment tracking, and release management across ADF and Databricks workloads.Designed Azure Synapse dimensional models for sales, inventory, product, supplier and customer analytics using fact and dimension tables.Optimized SQL and Spark workloads by tuning joins, partitioning, data skew, and query logic, reducing a high-volume retail transformation from approximately 50 minutes to under 15 minutes.Built the transformation framework that pulls together supplier, product catalog, and inventory data from a handful of source systems that didn't always agree with each other on product IDs   spent a lot of time on entity resolution logic here.Worked with MongoDB for semi-structured product, supplier, and inventory data, supporting ingestion and downstream analytics workflows.Wrote PySpark jobs against multi-terabyte sales/inventory tables; built out star-schema models that the BI team's Power BI reports still run on.Developed reusable enterprise data warehouse structures integrating retail transaction, inventory and product master data for Power BI reporting.Worked with Delta Lake tables in Azure Databricks to manage sales, inventory, supplier, and product datasets used by downstream analytics teams.Used Spark SQL and PySpark to transform multi-terabyte retail datasets and prepare curated data for merchandising and supply-chain reporting.Applied medallion-style data architecture using Delta Lake across raw, transformed, and curated layers, improving data quality and reuse for downstream analytics.Used Azure Stream Analytics to process near-real-time retail event data and support timely availability of operational datasets for downstream reporting.Built reusable PySpark and Spark SQL ETL transformations in Databricks for multi-terabyte datasets, including joins, aggregations, cleansing, validation, and incremental processing.Developed Python-based data processing routines to extract and transform MongoDB documents before loading curated datasets into Azure data platforms.Integrated MongoDB product, supplier, and inventory collections with Azure data pipelines, performing source-to-target validation before loading curated datasets into Databricks and Synapse.Optimized Synapse SQL queries and large analytical tables through partitioning, distribution strategy and query tuning.Fixed a recurring data-skew problem on one of our biggest join jobs (a few SKUs had wildly disproportionate transaction volume) by salting the join key   took the job from ~50 min to under 15.Built automated validation checks comparing row counts and key aggregates between source and target after each load; alerted the team via email/Teams when something looked off instead of waiting for someone downstream to notice.Partnered with merchandising and business teams to understand reporting requirements, investigate data discrepancies, and ensure datasets were available for seasonal planning and operational decisions.Helped validate data during a legacy warehouse-to-cloud migration   mostly writing comparison queries and chasing down discrepancies with the DBA team.Performed data validation and reconciliation between MongoDB source collections and downstream Databricks datasets to identify missing or inconsistent records.Built the datasets behind several exec-level Power BI dashboards used in weekly merchandising reviews; iterated on these a lot based on feedback from stakeholders who weren't shy about pointing out what was missing.Used Azure Key Vault to securely manage credentials and connection information for Azure data integration workflows.Developed dimensional and semantic datasets supporting Power BI reporting, aligning business definitions, reusable measures, and analytical models with merchandising requirements.Implemented Azure Key Vault for secure management of credentials and connection information used by data integration workflows.Performed source-to-target validation, reconciliation, and root-cause analysis for pipeline and data-quality issues, resolving discrepancies with source-system and DBA teams.Set up basic pipeline monitoring/alerting so failed ADF jobs got flagged before someone opened a support ticket asking where their report was.Environment: Azure Data Factory, Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS Gen2), PySpark, Spark SQL, Azure SQL Database, Synapse Analytics, Python, Power BI, Git, Azure DevOps, SQL ServerHadoop / Big Data EngineerVerizon | Irving, TX	Jun 2016   Dec 2017Joined the network analytics team as they were moving reporting off Oracle onto Hadoop   mostly wrote ingestion and transformation jobs for customer usage, billing, and network performance data.Redesigned a handful of the largest Hive tables with proper partitioning (by date) and bucketing (by subscriber ID) after query times on the old flat tables were getting complaints from the analytics team.Wrote Hive and Spark jobs against usage/billing/network datasets that ran into the multi-terabyte range; helped plan out the HDFS directory structure and retention policy for the growing data lake.Implemented Kafka ingestion patterns for network-event streams and validated incoming event data before downstream processing.Used Sqoop to pull data out of Oracle into Hadoop on a recurring schedule; tuned split-by columns and parallelism so imports didn't hammer the source database during business hours.Developed Hive-based dimensional data marts for customer usage, network performance and revenue analytics using partitioned and bucketed tables.Used Spark SQL and Hive queries to transform large customer usage, billing, and network-performance datasets stored across HDFS.Worked with HBase for selected high-volume datasets where access patterns required faster lookups than traditional Hive tables.Tuned Kafka ingestion settings for network-event feeds to handle increasing event volumes without affecting the existing batch workloads.Worked with Oracle-to-Hadoop ingestion through Sqoop, validating source-to-target counts and resolving discrepancies during scheduled loads.Built Oozie workflows to chain together the Sqoop imports, Hive transforms, and downstream jobs   this was before Airflow was really an option on our stack.Optimized large-scale Hive queries through partition pruning, bucketing and query-plan tuning across multi-terabyte telecom datasets.Set up a basic Kafka ingestion pipeline for a subset of near-real-time network events, which was fairly new territory for the team at the time.Built out several Hive data marts for churn analysis and revenue reporting that the ops reporting team used directly.Worked with network engineering on service-quality datasets   mostly translating what they wanted to see operationally into something that could actually be queried at scale.Built batch ingestion workflows using Sqoop and Oozie, coordinating Oracle-to-HDFS ingestion, Hive transformations and downstream reporting jobs.FHelped the QA team validate a few large migrations from the old reporting system, mostly spot-checking row counts and aggregates against known-good numbers.Environment: Hadoop, HDFS, Hive, Pig, Sqoop, Oozie, Spark, Kafka, HBase, Python, Shell Scripting, Oracle, Unix/Linux, GitETL Developer / Junior Data EngineerState Farm Insurance | Bloomington, IL	May 2015   May 2016First job out of the gate on the policy/claims reporting team   started out mostly maintaining existing SSIS packages before getting to build new ones.Built parameterized SSIS packages to load policy administration, claims, and customer data from several source systems into SQL Server staging and reporting databases.Put together reusable ETL templates so the underwriting and claims reporting teams didn't need a new package built from scratch every time they onboarded a new report.Used T-SQL to develop stored procedures, views, and transformation logic for policy, claims, and customer reporting datasets.Worked with SQL Server Agent to schedule recurring ETL jobs and configured failure notifications for overnight claims and policy data loads.Used SSIS package variables, parameters, and error-handling components to make recurring insurance data loads easier to maintain.Developed SQL Server data warehouse staging, fact and dimension structures for policy, claims and customer reporting.Supported SSRS reporting for claims operations by validating source data, report queries, and calculated measures before deployment.Worked with Oracle source data during insurance reporting feeds and validated extracts before loading them into SQL Server staging tables.Wrote stored procedures, views, and a fair amount of T-SQL for reporting   learned a lot about query tuning from a senior DBA who reviewed most of my early work.Implemented CDC-based incremental loads on a couple of the larger claims tables after the nightly full-refresh jobs started running past their maintenance window.Built SSRS reports for the claims operations team and helped out on a few SSAS cubes, though that was more the senior developer's area   I mostly supported.Spent a good amount of time on data profiling and cleansing   finding duplicate policy records, inconsistent date formats, that sort of thing   before it became a bigger production issue.Added logging and error handling to the older SSIS packages that didn't have any, which made troubleshooting failed loads much less of a guessing game.Built incremental warehouse loads using CDC-based processing for high-volume claims and policy tables to reduce nightly full-refresh processing.Wrote PowerShell scripts to automate a few recurring manual processes (file archiving, log cleanup) and set up SQL Agent jobs with failure email alerts.Sat in on Agile ceremonies (standups, sprint planning, retros) and got comfortable estimating and scoping my own ETL tasks by the second half of the year.Implemented source-to-target reconciliation and data-quality checks across Oracle source systems and SQL Server warehouse tables.Helped document a few of the ETL workflows and wrote basic runbooks   useful since I was often the one who got asked how something worked six months later.Environment: SQL Server, SSIS, SSRS, SSAS, T-SQL, PowerShell, Excel, Windows Server, Oracle, SQL Developer, Team Foundation Server (TFS)EDUCATION[JNTUH College of Engineering Hyderabad-Bachelor Of Technology (B.Tech)   Computer Science & Engineering-computers science and engineering - 2014 resumeText:
Srikanth G

Senior Data Engineer 

Phone: +1 (708) 320 - 9499

Email: srikanthg9457@gmail.com





PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

Senior Data Engineer with 13+ years of experience designing, architecting, and delivering enterprise-scale batch and real-time data platforms across AWS cloud and distributed data ecosystems. Extensive expertise in building high-performance streaming and batch processing solutions using Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, PySpark, Spark Streaming, AWS EMR, Lambda, S3, and event-driven architectures.

Proven experience leading end-to-end data platform modernization initiatives, including architecture design, framework development, data governance, performance optimization, and cloud-native engineering practices. Strong background in developing scalable streaming pipelines, real-time event processing systems, enterprise data lakes, and data warehouse solutions supporting mission-critical business operations.

Hands-on expertise in designing Kafka-based event streaming platforms, developing Flink stream processing applications, implementing PySpark batch workloads, and integrating enterprise systems through AWS services including S3, Lambda, EMR, EC2, Aurora PostgreSQL, Batch, and CloudWatch.

Experienced in driving engineering standards, code quality, CI/CD implementation, platform observability, reliability engineering, and mentoring development teams. Adept at collaborating with architects, business stakeholders, and engineering leadership to deliver secure, resilient, and cost-efficient data solutions.



Key strengths include:



Apache Kafka & Event Streaming Architecture

Apache Flink Real-Time Processing

PySpark & Spark Batch Processing

AWS Data Platform Architecture

AWS Lambda, EMR, EC2, Batch & S3

Aurora PostgreSQL & Data Modeling

Event-Driven Data Integration

Enterprise Data Lake & Warehousing

Performance Optimization & Scalability

Technical Leadership & Solution Architecture

Data Governance & Reliability Engineering



TECHNICAL SKILLS

Cloud Platforms: AWS (S3, EC2, EMR, Lambda, Glue, Redshift, Athena, Aurora PostgreSQL, Batch, MQ, Step Functions, CloudWatch, IAM, VPC), GCP (BigQuery, Dataproc, Dataflow, Cloud Storage, Composer)

Big Data & Distributed Processing:Apache Spark, PySpark, Spark SQL, Apache Flink, Hadoop, HDFS, MapReduce, Hive, Pig, Cloudera

Streaming & Messaging Technologies: Apache Kafka, Kafka Connect, Spark Streaming, Apache Flink Streaming, AWS MQ, Event-Driven Architecture, Real-Time Data Processing

Programming Languages: Python, PySpark, Scala, SQL, T-SQL, Shell Scripting

Data Warehousing & Analytics: Snowflake, Amazon Redshift, Google BigQuery, Teradata, Data Marts, Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW), OLAP

ETL / ELT & Data Integration: AWS Glue, Apache Airflow, Sqoop, SSIS, REST APIs, CDC (Change Data Capture), Kafka Connect, Batch Processing Frameworks

Databases: Aurora PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB

Data Modeling: Dimensional Modeling, Star Schema, Snowflake Schema, ER Modeling, Fact & Dimension Modeling, Data Vault, Medallion Architecture

Workflow Orchestration: Apache Airflow, Oozie, Control-M, AWS Step Functions

DevOps & CI/CD: Git, GitHub, Jenkins, Terraform, AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeBuild, CI/CD Automation

Monitoring & Observability: AWS CloudWatch, Grafana, Splunk, ELK Stack, Log Monitoring, Alerting & Incident Management

ERP & Enterprise Applications: SAP ECC, SAP HANA, SAP SD (Sales & Distribution), SAP Sales Orders, Deliveries, Shipments, Billing, Invoice Processing

Data Governance & Quality:Data Validation, Data Reconciliation, Data Quality Frameworks, Metadata Management, Alation, Reltio MDM

Reporting & Visualization: Tableau, Power BI, SSRS, Crystal Reports

Development Tools: GitHub, JIRA, Postman, SQL Developer, SSMS, Erwin Data Modeler

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE



BigCommerce – Atlanta, GA

Senior Data Engineer 

Jan 2024 – Present

Led the design and implementation of a cloud-native data platform on AWS supporting both real-time and batch data processing requirements across e-commerce domains.

Worked closely with solution architects, product owners, and business stakeholders to define scalable data platform architecture and integration strategies.

Designed Kafka-based event streaming solutions to capture customer, order, payment, inventory, and shipment events from multiple source applications.

Developed Apache Flink streaming applications to perform real-time data validation, enrichment, aggregation, and event correlation.

Built PySpark-based batch processing frameworks on AWS EMR for large-scale transformation and loading of transactional and analytical datasets.

Designed and maintained AWS S3-based data lake architecture supporting raw, curated, and business-ready data layers.

Implemented event-driven integrations using Kafka, AWS Lambda, and AWS services to support near real-time business reporting and downstream applications.

Designed Aurora PostgreSQL schemas and optimized data models to support high-volume transactional and analytical workloads.

Established reusable Python frameworks for ingestion, validation, exception handling, logging, and monitoring across multiple data pipelines.

Led technical design reviews and code reviews to ensure adherence to engineering standards and platform best practices.

Implemented CI/CD pipelines using GitHub, Jenkins, and Infrastructure-as-Code practices to automate deployments across environments.

Partnered with DevOps teams to establish monitoring, alerting, observability, and operational support processes using CloudWatch.

Optimized Kafka consumer throughput, Flink checkpointing strategies, and Spark job performance to improve reliability and reduce infrastructure costs.

Mentored junior engineers and provided technical guidance on distributed systems, AWS services, Kafka, Flink, and PySpark development.

Supported production releases, incident resolution, root cause analysis, and continuous platform improvement initiatives.







Highmark Health – Atlanta, GA

Senior Data Engineer 

Sept 2022 – Jan 2024

Designed and developed AWS-based healthcare data processing solutions supporting claims, member, provider, and operational analytics.

Built scalable ingestion pipelines using AWS Glue, Kafka, and PySpark to process structured and semi-structured healthcare datasets.

Developed PySpark applications on AWS EMR to perform large-scale transformations, data quality checks, and business rule validations.

Implemented Kafka-based event ingestion frameworks supporting real-time healthcare data exchange across enterprise systems.

Designed and maintained AWS S3 data lake architecture to support enterprise reporting and analytics initiatives.

Developed data reconciliation frameworks to ensure consistency between source systems and analytical platforms.

Built automated workflows using Apache Airflow to orchestrate ingestion, transformation, validation, and loading processes.

Implemented CI/CD practices and deployment automation to improve release management and reduce operational overhead.

Collaborated with business teams to define KPIs, data definitions, and reporting requirements for enterprise dashboards.

Participated in performance tuning efforts for Spark workloads and database queries to improve processing efficiency.

Supported data governance, compliance, auditing, and security requirements within healthcare data environments.



Neiman Marcus – Dallas, TX

Senior Data Engineer 

June 2020 – Sept 2022

Developed AWS-based retail analytics solutions supporting sales, inventory, order fulfillment, and customer behavior reporting.

Designed and implemented scalable data ingestion pipelines using AWS S3, Kafka, and PySpark.

Built data lake and Snowflake integration frameworks supporting enterprise reporting and advanced analytics.

Developed Spark-based transformation pipelines to process large retail transaction datasets and customer activity records.

Implemented near real-time ingestion patterns using Kafka and event-driven processing techniques.

Designed dimensional models and curated datasets supporting executive reporting and operational dashboards.

Collaborated with cross-functional teams to identify data requirements and optimize analytical workflows.

Improved performance of Spark jobs and Snowflake workloads through partitioning, clustering, and query optimization techniques.

Participated in deployment planning, production support, and platform modernization initiatives.





Macy’s – Atlanta, GA

Senior Data Engineer 

June 2019 – May 2020

Developed enterprise data pipelines on AWS supporting retail sales, inventory, shipment, and customer analytics.

Built Spark and PySpark applications for processing large volumes of structured and semi-structured data.

Designed AWS S3 data lake structures and data transformation frameworks supporting reporting and analytics requirements.

Developed ETL processes using AWS Glue and Spark to standardize and integrate data from multiple source systems.

Implemented data quality validation and reconciliation processes to ensure reporting accuracy.

Worked with business stakeholders to gather requirements and deliver analytical datasets for reporting solutions.

Optimized SQL queries and Spark workloads to improve processing performance and resource utilization.



Regions Bank – GA

Big Data Engineer

June 2017 – May 2019

Collaborated with business stakeholders and subject matter experts to gather data requirements and design scalable big data processing pipelines supporting enterprise analytics and reporting needs.

Designed and developed distributed data processing workflows using Hadoop ecosystem technologies including Cloudera, HDFS, MapReduce, Hive, and Apache Spark to process large volumes of structured and semi-structured datasets.

Built high-performance Spark applications using Scala and Spark SQL to ingest and transform data from relational databases and streaming platforms.

Developed real-time streaming pipelines using Apache Kafka and Spark Streaming to process event- driven data and persist processed datasets into Cassandra for downstream applications and analytics.

Implemented data preprocessing frameworks using Spark DataFrames to transform complex nested JSON and XML datasets into structured formats for analytics and reporting.

Led migration of on-premise big data workloads to AWS cloud infrastructure, utilizing Amazon EC2 for compute and Amazon S3 for scalable data storage.

Built scalable data ingestion pipelines to transfer data from RDBMS systems into Hadoop and Cassandra environments, enabling large-scale distributed data processing.

Developed and optimized MapReduce, Hive, and Pig workflows to process large enterprise datasets while improving performance using partitioning, compression, and bucketing techniques.

Designed and maintained analytical datasets and reporting tables in Teradata and Snowflake, enabling business intelligence teams to build dashboards and reports using Tableau.

Automated data pipeline scheduling and monitoring using Oozie workflows, while tracking development tasks and production issues using JIRA and version control systems.

Designed enterprise event streaming architecture using Apache Kafka supporting fraud monitoring, transaction processing, and customer activity tracking.

Developed real-time Spark Streaming applications consuming Kafka topics and processing high-volume financial transaction events.

Built resilient producer-consumer frameworks with fault tolerance, retry mechanisms, and message delivery guarantees.

Implemented event-driven integrations between Hadoop, Cassandra, Teradata, and enterprise banking systems.

Led performance tuning of streaming applications and Kafka clusters to support mission-critical workloads.



V Consultancy Services – Hyderabad, India



SQL Server Developer 

Sept 2011 – Nov 2015

Project 1: First American Title Insurance Company:

Translated business needs into data analysis, business intelligence data sources and reporting solutions for different types of information consumers.

Involved in Planning, Defining and Designing data base using Erwin on business requirement and provided documentation.

Developed complex T-SQL code such as Stored Procedures, functions, triggers, Indexes and views for the application.

Used Joins, correlated and non-correlated sub-queries for complex business queries involving multiple tables & calculations from different databases.

Created SSIS package to load data from XML Files and SQL Server 2005 to SQL Server 2008 by using Lookup, Fuzzy Lookup, Derived Columns, Condition Split, Term Extraction, Aggregate, Pivot Transformation, and Slowly Changing Dimension.

Converted Crystal Reports to SQL Server Reports.

Used SSIS to create ETL packages to Validate, Extract, Transform and Load data to Data Warehouse and Data Mart Databases.

Developed Unit Test Plans for SSIS packages for checking the functionality of each component.

Modified the existing SSIS packages to meet the changes specified by the users.

Scheduled Jobs for executing the stored SSIS packages which were developed to update the database on Daily basis using SQL Server Agent.

Project 2: Charter Communications:

Gathered user requirements to develop the business logic and analyzed and designed database solutions.

Generated Performance reports on SSIS packages, Stored Procedures and Triggers.

Created OLAP cubes using SSAS to analyze the business condition of the sales.

Wrote complex queries for the drill down reports and used conditional formatting using SSRS.

Used SSIS to transfer data from various sources like SQL Server, MS Access to be used for generating reports using SSRS 2008.

Formatted reports for various Output formats as requested by the management using SSRS.

Actively supported business users for changes in reports as and when required using SSRS.

Analyzed reports and fixed bugs in stored procedures using SSRS.

Created linked reports and managed snapshots using SSRS.

Performed various calculations using complex expressions in the reports and created report models.

Designed and optimized indexes, views, stored procedures and functions using T-SQL.

Performed maintenance duties like performance tuning and optimization of queries, functions and stored procedures.

Designed high level SSIS architecture for overall data transfer from the source server to the Enterprise Services Warehouse.



EDUCATION
